objectives: Differentiate uncomplicated acute otitis media from dangerous ear infection signs.
Use fever, ear findings, and child behavior to choose treatment intensity.
Counsel caregivers on pain control, antibiotics adherence when indicated, and return signs.
takeaways: A bulging or inflamed tympanic membrane with fever and ear pain supports acute otitis media.
No mastoid swelling or systemic danger signs supports HC III outpatient care.
Follow-up and return precautions are essential because ear infection can progress.
learnCaseOverrides.blurb: A toddler with ear pain and fever needs careful ear exam and practical outpatient planning.

sections.title: Chief complaint
sections.text: Right ear pain with fever for 2 days

sections.title: Caregiver concern
sections.text: Child cries when lying on the right side and pulls the ear repeatedly.

coach.title: Ivan is crying but still drinking fluids
coach.body: First rule out severe disease, then treat likely acute otitis media appropriately.

sections.title: Ear findings
sections.text: Right tympanic membrane is red and bulging; no mastoid tenderness or swelling.

coach.title: Which diagnosis fits best?
coach.body: Use the ear exam and danger-sign findings together.

question.prompt: What is the most likely classification?

options.text: Acute otitis media without mastoiditis signs
No ear disease because child has fever

question.right: Correct. Bulging inflamed tympanic membrane with ear pain and fever supports AOM; no mastoid swelling lowers immediate referral urgency.
question.wrong: Ignoring clear ear findings can miss treatable AOM. Severe referral signs like mastoid swelling are absent here.

sections.title: Treatment bundle
sections.detail: Analgesia +/- oral antibiotic per guideline, hydration, fever care

sections.title: Escalate if
sections.reveal_note: Caregiver agrees to return if danger signs appear.

coach.title: What is the safest next action?
coach.body: Choose a realistic HC III plan.

question.prompt: How should you manage this child now?

options.text: Treat likely AOM with pain control and guideline-based oral therapy, then review in 2 days
Use ear candling and reassure only
Start IV antibiotics immediately for every ear infection
Discharge without return precautions once pain improves

question.right: Correct. This child is stable and fits uncomplicated AOM, so outpatient treatment and close review are appropriate.
question.wrong: Either overtreatment or absent follow-up can harm outcomes. AOM needs practical treatment plus explicit return instructions.

sections.title: Case outcome
sections.text: You diagnosed probable acute otitis media and provided safe outpatient management with warning signs.
sections.emphasis: Ear exam details changed treatment confidence.

coach.title: Key teaching points
coach.body: For febrile ear pain in children, combine otoscopic findings with danger-sign screening. Most stable AOM can be managed at HC III with close follow-up.
